openings.claim: Does the incumbent have an attainable pressure range that simultaneously prevents sliding and avoids rocking, especially with the right-contact card?
openings.delta: Change the acceptance dependency from presumed balanced tightening to measured corner response. Keep the paired-strip carrier; challenge its pressure-to-friction action before accepting it.
openings.prediction: The nearest rival explanation is that added normal force restrains sliding only by transferring load away from the opposite corner. It predicts reduced sliding accompanied by corner lift, possibly worsened by the card. A usable pressure range predicts both position within 1 mm and no damaging lift; neither is established.
openings.probe: First measure whether strip lengths, bolt clearance and rim access permit capture and complete withdrawal without fixture alteration. If feasible within ninety minutes, use one clamp configuration for ten numbered opening/closure/20 N pull trials within twenty minutes, with the final right-contact card. Record position, corner lift, release time and visible seal tears each cycle. Persistent lift accompanying reduced sliding defeats the balanced-pressure explanation; outcome failure rejects this configuration. Stop on tears. These measurements can expose coupling but cannot establish that every possible tightening setting fails.
assumptions: Accessible underside geometry, sufficient strip stiffness and recoverable cord retention remain unverified.
No new materials, extra trials or fixture modification; deployment awaits all valued outcome checks.

assessment: Two incumbent dependencies warrant attack. Geometry may prevent fabrication altogether; the supplied rocking observation directly weakens the safe-friction assumption. A single probe preserves the outcome and constraints without inventing a replacement or a feasible pressure range.

lineage.reason: Recast the clamp proposal as a falsifiable concern about geometry and pressure coupling; its performance remains unproven.

attacks.dependency: Paired strips can capture an accessible underside with outboard bolt clearance. The rim profile is unspecified; dimensional inspection must precede fabrication.
Balanced modest pressure can supply adequate friction without rocking or seal damage. The three supplied corner-lift trials challenge this dependency; the disturbed cycle tests its vulnerability.
